<description>
Backports:
* #35168

`v31.1` still carries the pre-fix `LoadBlockIndex`, which re-adds a pruned block to `m_blocks_unlinked` when its parent is header-only (#35050). On the next block connected, `CheckBlockIndex` hits `Assertion failed: (!foundInUnlinked)`. `-checkblockindex` is on by default only on regtest, so this crashes functional-test suites run against 31.x, not mainnet nodes.

Both commits cherry-pick cleanly with `-x`. The only difference from master is the surrounding context in `test_runner.py`. The added `feature_prune_stale_fork.py` fails against the `v31.1` release binary on the assertion above and passes on this branch (2/2 each, macOS arm64, built from `depends`).

I left the release-notes entry to whoever assembles the 31.x notes.
</description>

<commits>
6cedc5d47e validation: Don't add pruned blocks to m_blocks_unlinked on startup

LoadBlockIndex() adds to m_blocks_unlinked based only on nTx > 0, without
checking BLOCK_HAVE_DATA. Pruning preserves nTx but clears BLOCK_HAVE_DATA,
so a pruned block whose parent was header-only gets re-added on every
restart, causing the CheckBlockIndex() assertion that entries must have
data on disk to fail.

Check that BLOCK_HAVE_DATA is set before inserting into m_blocks_unlinked.

Fixes #35050.

(cherry picked from commit 0e4b0bacecf94063342c7f9eb9b03dac8a7a7936)

5ec487b9ae test: Add coverage for m_blocks_unlinked invariant in LoadBlockIndex

A pruned stale-fork block whose parent doesn't have any transactions
shouldn't be added to m_blocks_unlinked when starting up a node.

(cherry picked from commit 3f44f9aef7ccd0417fcd0c2f33f20615ea5c11e6)
</commits>
